description: The Department of Justice released a second major document dump following up on the Epstein Files Transparency Act.
headline: Department of Justice Releases Second Major File Dump Pertaining to the Epstein Files Transparency Act

info.description: The Department of Justice's Office of the Deputy Attorney General sent out a press release accompanying the release of this selection documents.
info.note: This press release included the disclaimer that, "Some of the documents contain untrue and sensationalist claims against President Trump that were submitted to the FBI right before the 2020 election. To be clear, the claims are unfounded and false, and if they have a shred of credibility, they certainly would have been weaponized against President Trump already."

info.description: The Department of Justice released this set of documents far after the original 2025-12-19 due date.
info.note: The Department of Justice did not appear to publicly comment again on the missed date.

info.description: An FBI Complaint Form was filed matching the content of Katie Johnson's lawsuit.
info.note: That lawsuit was originally filed in June 2016, with the FBI complaint dating to July 2016. The FBI complaint details the filed lawsuit.

info.description: Epstein seemingly drafted emails to Bill Gates in July 2013 concerning Bill's "disregard[ing] and discard[ing] of our friendship." The emails appear emotionally charged. The first email draft that day refers to  Beyond quoting business differences, the second email draft later that day refers to Epstein accusing Bill of asking him to delete email correspondence "regarding your std, your request that I provide you antibiotics that you can surreptitiously give to Melinda, and the description of your penis". It is unclear if the emails that Epstein is referring to exist, or if they would have been deleted.
info.note: Esptein cites Bill Gates' now-ex-wife Melinda as a contributing factor in their declined relationship, which aligns with Melinda's statement that Bill's friendship with Epstein was a factor in their deteriorated marriage. The emails Epstein mentions do not, at least as-of-yet, appear in the Epstein files.

info.description: The release included bank records and correspondence concerning Peter Mandelson, then the former UK ambassador to the United States.
info.note: The records indicate three transfers from Epstein totalling $75,000 to accounts linked to Mandelson or his partner between 2003 and 2004. Correspondence in the release was reported to show Mandelson relaying UK government information to Epstein, including asset sales and tax changes under consideration in 2009 and plans for the 2010 eurozone bailout. Mandelson said he had no recollection of the payments and questioned the documents' authenticity. The material led the UK government to refer the matter to the Metropolitan Police.
